svg.title: Case 2: headquarters assumed Unification while the facts pointed to Diversification, and the architecture each assumption produces
svg.desc: Two panels at the top contrast the assumed operating model, Unification with unified IP planning, unified security policy and a unified egress, with the actual one, Diversification with independent units plus a few shared services at most moving towards Coordination. A four row table then pairs each business unit with its real characteristic and what unification broke: auto parts with EDI over a carrier the customer names against a unified egress that cannot be implemented, home appliance parts with its own e-commerce against a change chain that is too long, tooling with two hundred people and a part-time IT role against a platform nobody can carry, and a new energy plant sharing almost no data against a build slowed by a forced architecture. The corrected design unifies only the shared internet egress, the group security baseline and the WAN transport framework, while each unit keeps its addressing and change authority and layered templates replace the one size fits all.
svg.text: Case 2: “the group is therefore Unification” was the whole design error
Five business units, one headquarters assumption, and three of the five standards failed on contact with reality
assumed: Unification
unified IP planning · unified security policy
· unified internet egress, pushed to every unit
the model headquarters wanted to be true
actual: Diversification, trending to Coordination
independent units plus a few shared services
(low standardisation, low integration)
the model the two questions actually returned
BUSINESS UNIT
REAL CHARACTERISTIC
WHAT UNIFICATION BROKE
auto parts
EDI with OEMs; the circuit must use the carrier the customer names
the unified egress cannot be implemented at all
home appliance parts
runs its own e-commerce; needs fast CDN and cloud changes
the change approval chain is far too long
tooling
200 people; IT is a part-time role
nobody can carry a unified management platform
new energy
a brand-new plant sharing almost no data with the group
forcing the architecture into the build slows the plant
THE CORRECTED DESIGN · UNIFY THREE THINGS, LET THE REST BE LOCAL
shared internet egress
bought once, consumed by every unit
group security baseline
mandatory, auditable, not negotiable
WAN transport framework
which carriers, which paths, which SLA
each unit keeps its own addressing plan and its own change authority — that is what Diversification means in practice
layered policy templates replace the one-size-fits-all: a mandatory security baseline plus optional network templates
Get the operating model wrong and every downstream design is wrong: the units were not being difficult, they were being described by a model nobody had checked.
